Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 (REC-vc-data-integrity-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own (README.md gives the search). Source .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.bin, sha256 ba5c4baf13fe3bab3ebd95ab6650d6fe83720e254b383bb444b4fbbae7bcf4fe; quotations are cut from its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.txt, sha256 2b7725f80e138ef943eff25050eee6a62f8887762ca9e1e03867c55ea5647beb, and cite its line numbers (L). LEVELS: the root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules, so a failure there is non-conformance; an anchor ending in -should adds SHOULD statements and includes the root by reference, so a failure there is a warning. MAY statements are never constraints: a leniency a MAY grants has its own anchor, named for the leniency. A constraint marked INFERRED is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source; one marked OUTSIDE-SOURCE comes from a document the source names and is not this source's. Rule ids (P-nn, S-nn, V-nn, E-nn, O-nn, M-nn) are those of rules.derived.yaml. INSTANCE: a verification method as it sits in a controlled identifier document (section 2.1 verificationMethod; section 2.6). This source defines NO verification method type: the value of the verificationMethod property points to one (“This public key data is stored in a controlled identifier document, which contains a full description of the verification method.” (L211)), and Multikey and JsonWebKey, which its contexts (I-04) map, were moved to Controlled Identifiers v1.0 (revision history L950: “Moved Multikey definitions to controlled identifier document.” (L950)). ROOT = only what this source says of a verification method: controller (L484), expires and revocation (L486). ANCHORS #multikey-cid and #jsonwebkey-cid are OUTSIDE-SOURCE: the members Controlled Identifiers v1.0 (fetched 2026-11-07, sha256 c5e9befba602b53de46669cf98067123d1901357a425f8bff621796b2ac4ac4a) gives each type; they bind nothing in this source.
title: A verification method referenced by a proof (DERIVED)

controller.$comment: M-01 “matches the URL value used to identify the issuer or holder” (L484) (no keyword). A URL string when present. Controlled Identifiers v1.0 states its own MUST for the controller value (OUTSIDE-SOURCE); the URL syntax is the WHATWG one, approximated here as in P-01.

expires.$comment: M-02 “The revocation and expiration times for a verification method are expressed using the revocation and expires properties, respectively” (L486) (no keyword). The type is not stated in this source; a date-time is INFERRED from times, with or without an offset.

revocation.$comment: M-03 as M-02 (L486). The same section's revision history (L972) calls the property revoked: “Added revoked and expires to verification methods.” (L972) README T-03. Controlled Identifiers v1.0 names it revoked.

revoked.$comment: M-04 the revision-history spelling (L972); see M-03.

multikey.$comment: ANCHOR #multikey-cid. OUTSIDE-SOURCE (Controlled Identifiers v1.0, section 2.2.2): type Multikey, publicKeyMultibase.

jwk.$comment: ANCHOR #jsonwebkey-cid. OUTSIDE-SOURCE (Controlled Identifiers v1.0, section 2.2.3): type JsonWebKey, publicKeyJwk, a JSON object.
